title: Safe to Serve: Aligning Instruction-Tuned Models for Safety and Helpfulness
measurement_description: The paper measures the generation of unsafe, harmful, or hateful content in response to prompts targeting religious groups. This is evaluated as part of a broader assessment of model safety.
findings: The study found that instruction-tuning with a small number of safety-related examples (Safety Instruction-Tuning) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) significantly reduced the generation of harmful responses to unsafe prompts, including those targeting religious groups like Muslims and Jews. The baseline model often generated unsafe content that supported harmful premises, whereas the safety-aligned models learned to refuse such prompts or provide a safe, neutral response, increasing the percentage of safe responses from approximately 40% to over 90%.
